title: Symmetric cryptography: AES, modes of operation and the initialisation vector

videos.script: Vereda keeps a referral letter for every patient, and the letter has to be stored encrypted. {{title}} AES is the cipher nearly everybody uses for that, and choosing it is the easy part. {{aes}} The hard part is everything around it. Here is Monday's appointment file, encrypted with AES and a good key. {{ecb}} Without the key, you can still see which slots are booked. Same key, same cipher, a different mode, and the pattern is gone. {{cbc}} Encrypt the same letter twice and you get the same bytes twice, unless the initialisation vector changes. {{iv}} And an encrypted file can still be altered without anybody noticing, unless the mode checks it. {{gcm}} This lesson is those four decisions: the cipher, the mode, the vector and the check.
